mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, investors anticipate higher future inflation, which lowers real equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (current value + 0.25%) in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the identified FEDFUNDS rise, or inflation surprises are not stronger than expected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 2,000 monthly for two consecutive months predicts stronger consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the employment surge, or GDP growth is not materially higher than average.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (goods orders) grows faster than CPIAUCSL (inflation) over the next quarter, it indicates strong nominal demand that outpaces price pressures, resulting in positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate over next 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when the condition holds, or inflation surprise is larger than demand surprise.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of 5% or more in a month signals supply-side weakness, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the INDPRO decline, or production rebounds unexpectedly quickly.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for two consecutive months, it suggests a tight labor market, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady and supporting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.05) during the low-unemployment period, or Fed hikes rates unexpectedly.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST (housing starts) and PAYEMS (employment) by at least 10% over the next month indicates improving housing demand and labor market strength, which together drive positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > (current * 1.1) AND PAYEMS > (current * 1.1) in the following month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the interaction, or one variable recovers while the other stagnates.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS > 5%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to expectations of future rate cuts and reduced growth, regardless of other signals.
regime_hint: High FED Funds rate steady state
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative over 10 such months, or macroeconomic data show robust growth consistent with high rates.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 8% in a month, it indicates weak consumer demand and supply chain easing, which typically precedes S&P 500 declines in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the RSAFS decline, or consumer confidence rebounds unexpectedly.
